Summary
Data source overview: The paper introduces Action Schema Networks (ASNets), a graph-convolutional neural architecture that shares weights across action schemas to learn generalised policies for probabilistic and classical planning. It analyses failure modes such as poor generalisation, limited receptive field and low interpretability, and presents architectural, regularisation and training improvements validated on seven benchmark domains.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[83]
The extraction follows the mandated causal-interventional pathway template, decomposes all introduced frameworks into white–box components and removes isolated nodes. Confidence is reduced mainly by the need to compress >20 000 words into ≈26 nodes while preserving every nuance.

Instruction-set improvement: 1) Explicitly ask the extractor to output a short table of all section titles seen—this would ease traceability checking. 2) Add an example showing how to merge multiple risk branches back into shared validation evidence nodes.

Inference strategy justification: Moderate inference (edge confidence 2) was used where the paper motivates an intervention implicitly (e.g. recommending LM-cut teacher use) but does not state it as an explicit actionable step.

Extraction completeness: All four central risks discussed (generalisation, interpretability, receptive-field limits, teacher sub-optimality) are followed through methods, findings and finally to clearly scoped interventions, yielding a fully connected fabric.

Key limitations: 1) The paper’s broader societal AI-safety implications (e.g. deployment in critical autonomy) are out of scope so risk nodes stay technical. 2) Numerical hyper-parameter tweaks are not promoted to separate intervention nodes as evidence on safety value is thin.
